name: Value-Smart Sandra
summary: Sandra is the most reachable segment for Visa. She will pay up to CHF 10/month if the benefit is clear, simple, and family-relevant. Grocery cashback is the strongest trigger. She already uses a credit card occasionally — the goal is to make Visa her primary card for family spending.

price_sensitivity.finding: Fee-conscious but not fee-allergic. Will pay CHF 8/month for foreign fee waiver if family travel spend justifies it — she does the math before deciding.
price_sensitivity.key_quote: I would quickly estimate our yearly travel spend to be sure the CHF 96 fee is really justified.
tags: opts out of CHF 5/mo if no clear benefit

feature_preference.finding: 2% grocery cashback is the clear winner — directly reduces the family's biggest recurring expense. Travel insurance is secondary. One-time bonuses are dismissed.
feature_preference.key_quote: I prefer something simple and ongoing that I can see every month.

behavior_switching.finding: Will switch for supermarket spending if cashback is clear and automatic. Explicitly says she would limit the card to grocery use and not complicate everything else.
behavior_switching.key_quote: A straightforward cashback that I can see on our grocery spending would convince me.

trade_off.finding: Mathematically rational but skeptical of marketing claims. Accepts net gain only if savings come from normal family spending — not special offers or extra effort.

willingness_to_pay.finding: CHF 10/month is the hard ceiling, only with clear ongoing benefits, strong security, and purchase protection. Would keep a free card as travel/online backup.
willingness_to_pay.key_quote: CHF 10 is the absolute maximum, and only if the benefits clearly exceed that every month.

visa_recommendation.viable_product: Family cashback card — CHF 6–8/month fee with 2% on Migros/Coop + purchase protection + basic travel insurance
visa_recommendation.acquisition_trigger: Visible monthly grocery savings + security + simplicity
